**Visual observations from test image:**
- Multiple corn stalks shown in cross-section/longitudinal view
- Shredded fibrous pith with stringy vascular strands visible
- Middle stalk shows yellowish-green rind with dark black/brown mottled blotches on the exterior
- Some small black specks visible on tissue
- Gray-white disintegrating pith tissue

**Key matching features:**
- The middle stalk's rind shows dark, coalescing black blotches — matches "tan to reddish brown water-soaked lesions that turn dark brown to shiny black" of Anthracnose stalk rot
- Shredded brown/black pith with fibrous strands — matches "brown to black pith discoloration or shredded pith"
- The reference image top-right panel shows nearly identical shredded pith with black rind discoloration

This rules out Charcoal stalk rot (which would show uniform charcoal-gray pith with microsclerotia dust, not shiny black rind patches) and Diplodia stalk rot (which would show small distinct pycnidia without the shiny black rind).
